First viewport of find: heading, paragraph, full-width search, identical card grid; nothing that only this library would have.

Product-bound elements are content and mechanism: the 'Open' session calendar (tool day-chosen 1280-light) and the desk-volunteer copy voice. Named as the strongest material, but they sit in a portable frame (rubric anchor 1).

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: The detectors reported nothing, which is consistent with a clean, token-consistent page; none of my items are measurable by the current tells except possibly SLP-58. Verdicts unchanged.

findings.title: Every tool card uses the same wrench icon as its thumbnail
findings.description: All ten cards on find show an identical wrench glyph on a pale green square where a tool image would be. The thumbnail slot carries no information and reads as a placeholder; the two cordless drills, the ladder and the hedge trimmer look the same at a glance.
findings.impact: Members choosing a specific tool ('the drill with two batteries') may get no visual help distinguishing items, and the page is likely to read as unfinished, which weakens trust in a volunteer service.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the thumbnail is for: either real photographs of the library's own tools (which the desk can take) or remove the slot; do not keep a repeated stand-in.

findings.title: No identity layer: the frame is a default service form
findings.description: Across all five routes the identity is the name in bold body-size text beside a small wrench glyph; type, colour and layout match the category default for public booking flows. Nothing on find, basket, confirm or done is a focal point drawn from the library's world (membership card, the room at the community centre, the Saturday list).
findings.impact: Members, many older and arriving a few times a year, may not recognise the page as their library's, and the design gives no warmth to back the 'neighbourly' attribute.
findings.recommendation: Decide an identity floor from the library's own material (the membership card the green is said to come from, the desk, the room) and carry it on every surface without adding hero moments; the session calendar is the natural place for a signature.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar covers part of the pick-up calendar
findings.description: On the tool page the fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar sits over the calendar: at 1280 a full week row (11-17 Oct) is hidden behind it; at 375 it covers the explanation of 'Open' days and the chosen-day line.
findings.impact: Members may not see the session days or which day they picked until they scroll, on the page whose job is choosing that day.
findings.recommendation: Reserve space for the bar at the end of the content (or confine the sticky bar to narrow widths) so no task content is obscured; verify in a scrolled capture.

findings.title: Tool names truncated with ellipsis on phones, making the two drills identical
findings.description: At 375 card titles are cut to one line ('Cordless drill 18 V, co...') so the two-battery and one-battery drills read the same; availability badges wrap leaving 'Oct' alone on a second line.
findings.impact: On the phone, where most members reserve, they may open the wrong drill; the distinguishing words are exactly what is cut.
findings.recommendation: Let titles wrap at narrow widths and give the badge room to stay on one line (the thumbnail slot is the obvious space to reclaim).

findings.title: Search field placed below the whole tool list on phones
findings.description: At 375 the 'Search tools' field and filter button appear after all ten cards, though at 1280 they sit above the list.
findings.impact: Phone users with a tool in mind may scroll the whole list before finding search; as stock grows this cost grows.
findings.recommendation: Keep the source and visual order the same at every width, with search before the list.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions listed in reverse date order with an uneven 1+5 layout
findings.description: On basket at 1280 the sessions run from Wednesday 28 October down to Saturday 10 October; the first is a full-width card and the other five are narrow cards wrapping to three lines each.
findings.impact: Members looking for 'Saturday morning' may scan the wrong way and the irregular grid looks unfinished on the step where the choice is made.
findings.recommendation: Order sessions chronologically and use one consistent layout for all session options.

findings.title: Misaligned value columns in the tool details
findings.description: The tool page's details are two lists with different label widths: values of Category/Deposit/Available from start at ~224px, values of Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case at ~180px.
findings.impact: The ragged column undermines the 'careful' attribute and makes the specs harder to scan.
findings.recommendation: Use one details list with one label column.

findings.title: Done page keeps 'Basket (1)' and gives the reservation number no weight
findings.description: After confirming, the nav still reads 'Basket (1)', and reservation number FT-4471 is set in the same body style as the other rows; there is no visual sign of success.
findings.impact: Members may wonder whether the reservation went through and may not note the number to quote to the desk.
findings.recommendation: Clear the basket count on completion and decide which item on done is primary (the session and number to bring).

findings.title: Footer stops short leaving an empty band of ground at wide widths
findings.description: On basket, confirm and done at 1280 the footer ends mid-viewport and a flat band of page ground fills the rest of the screen.
findings.impact: Short pages look unfinished on desktop, the lunch-break use scene.
findings.recommendation: Make the page fill the viewport so the footer sits at the bottom on short pages.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the tint on 'available' badges but keeps it on later dates
findings.description: In dark mode, 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badges render as green text with no visible tint while later dates keep a grey tinted box, inverting the light theme's emphasis.
findings.impact: In dark mode, which many members use, the later-availability badges look more prominent than available ones.
findings.recommendation: Compose the dark badge pair so the available state stays the emphasised one.

strengths: The copy voice is specific and well judged: concrete, brief, desk-volunteer tone ('Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence', 'Nothing is paid online').
The pick-up calendar marking library sessions as 'Open' is drawn from the product's real constraint and is the best candidate for a signature.
One consistent token system (type, green, radius, borders) across all routes and both themes; one filled button per page.
keep: Keep the volunteer copy voice and the session-aware calendar; any identity work should build on them, not replace them.
